key_insight: DreamTrue makes robot video prediction more action-faithful by conditioning on rendered action trajectories in image space and correcting for dataset/calibration issues. It also reduces the usual bias toward only successful outcomes by using counterfactual post-training.
problem_solved: The paper tackles two major problems in robot world models: imprecise camera/robot calibration that weakens action following, and datasets that overrepresent successful interactions, causing overly optimistic predictions.
method: Render robot action trajectories into image-space conditions so the model can better track intended motion across different embodiments.
Apply offline geometric calibration to improve alignment between actions, views, and predicted motion.
Use counterfactual post-training to expose the model to alternative outcomes, improving robustness and realism beyond only successful demonstrations.
impact: This helps practitioners build robot world models that are more reliable for planning, simulation, and policy learning. Better action-faithful predictions can improve transfer across robots and reduce failure from misleadingly idealized video forecasts.

paper_title: DreamTrue: Action-Faithful Robot World Model with Counterfactual Post-Training
